hypothesis.hypothesis_text: Test one bounded source-grounded candidate without transferring formal authority to a development hint.

nearest_history_candidates.hypothesis_text: Modify `_swap` in `policies/baseline_modules/local_search.py` to score each cross-route one-for-one exchange with an exact O(1) directed boundary-edge delta instead of copying both routes and recomputing both full depot-to-depot distances for every tested pair. For customers `a` and `b`, compare the predecessor/a/successor and predecessor/b/successor arcs before and after substitution, retaining the current load tests, pair enumeration order, strict `_EPS` improvement condition, deadline polling, and recalculation/index rebuild only after a selected improving swap. This preserves the same feasible accepted swap state on completed scans, including with asymmetric distances, while reducing VNS evaluation work and freeing fixed-budget time for more search trajectories.
nearest_history_candidates.target_weakness: The current `_swap` materializes two trial customer lists and calls full `_route_distance` twice for every capacity-feasible cross-route pair, despite only local adjacent arcs changing. This occurs in embedded VNS under a budget-exhausting runtime model and limits completed search work.
nearest_history_candidates.expected_effect: Unchanged hard feasibility and fleet_violation, lower swap-neighborhood scoring overhead, more completed ALNS/VNS work, and lower final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible outputs.

nearest_history_candidates.hypothesis_text: Modify `_default_vns_operators` in `policies/baseline_modules/local_search.py` so that it does not run `_relocate` immediately before `_or_opt_1`. The source shows that both neighborhoods enumerate the same feasible cross-route one-customer relocation state: a one-customer segment, capacity-feasible destination positions, and a strictly improving move. Retain `_or_opt_1`, which also covers that state while sharing the segment-relocation implementation used by longer Or-opt moves. Eliminating the redundant no-improvement scan should release embedded-VNS time for additional destroy/repair trajectories without removing a feasible one-customer relocation transition. Capacity, coverage, route count, route-limit rejection, and incumbent handling remain unchanged.
nearest_history_candidates.target_weakness: The default VNS executes two overlapping cross-route single-customer relocation neighborhoods in sequence (`_relocate` then `_or_opt_1`), paying for a second scan whenever the first finds no improvement. In the fixed-budget solver this redundant VNS work can reduce the number of ALNS trajectories explored.
nearest_history_candidates.expected_effect: For unchanged fleet-feasible outputs, reduce embedded-VNS runtime and increase completed ALNS iterations; seek lower final total_distance only if paired final outcomes improve without structural-feasibility or fleet_violation regression.
